Tennis Majors

The 2026 US Open runs from Saturday August 23 to Sunday September 13 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows, Queens, New York City. With 22 days of competition and entertainment, including eight days of free grounds admission, this is the largest event schedule and most competition days in the US Open’s near-150-year history. The US Open features the world’s top players competing across men’s and women’s singles and doubles, as well as junior, wheelchair and quad divisions.

This year’s tournament takes place during Rosh Hashanah, which begins on the evening of September 11, and concludes with the men’s singles final on September 13 at 2 p.m. [...] The US Open runs through September 13, with the singles main draws beginning August 30.

### Top players team up for mixed doubles

Fans once again have an opportunity to see some of the world’s greatest players in unusual pairings before the singles and doubles main draws get underway.

Arthur Ashe Stadium features three U.S. stars getting their singles campaigns underway: Australian Open champion Madison Keys, former finalist Taylor Fritz, and 2023 US Open winner Coco Gauff.

The reigning Roland-Garros men's singles champion, top seed Alexander Zverev, also begins his title defence at Flushing Meadows.
